items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: I know he's used John Collins, Al Viola, and he used to have Ziggy Elman and Dave Barber and Herbie Hamer -- he had a lot of jazz musicians backing him.

ctx.x: Yeah. I was in the air.

Were there other musicians from the jazz world also working for Frank? I know he usually likes to have jazz musicians in the orchestra. I know he's used John Collins, Al Viola, and he used to have Ziggy Elman and Dave Barber and Herbie Hamer -- he had a lot of jazz musicians backing him. Were there other jazz people from jazz when you were working with him?

Well, when we worked with Sinatra, the band didn't do much, unless once in awhile, somebody had to take a little extra chorus, because Sinatra did the singing, and naturally, he didn't need anyone to back him up on something where he was playing a solo. The only one he used to once in awhile play something in the same recording was Sweets -- the trumpet player.

items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: this thing we did with Nat, with "After Midnight" that featured Stuff Smith, John Tizol, Willie Smith, Harry Edison, John Collins.

ctx.x: Maybe I will. I'll go out and shoot Nat Hentoff first, then I'll shoot Leonard. This is -- as I say, this is very disturbing. I can't understand this. You know, because I made records, two solos, like with the Nat -- this thing we did with Nat, with "After Midnight" that featured Stuff Smith, John Tizol, Willie Smith, Harry Edison, John Collins. And Nat. How can I -- you know, what is this? It's just amazing, I don't understand it.
